title: UMD complexity review: Dagster + Hatchet dual-orchestration is redundant in v1
body: Complexity review of the proposed Universal Media Decomposer API architecture (Option A). Finding F1 (MEDIUM confidence): Dagster is retained as a DAG/lineage declaration layer while Hatchet is the sole runner and Dagster auto-materialize/schedulers are disabled in production. The §16 lineage information Dogster would provide already exists twice: Hatchet DAG parents edges and stage-manifest input_refs/evidence_refs. Recommendation to DDAuthor: drop Dogster from v1, derive the invalidation lineage table from the single Hatchet DAG definition, reintroduce asset-freshness tooling only behind the projection interface when measured. Full review: artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-complexity-review.md

title: UMD complexity review: optional graph/RDF projections should be fenced out of v1 footprint
body: Finding F2 (MEDIUM-HIGH confidence): the architecture-options ownership map, repo structure, and footprint estimate (18-24 packages) carry Neo4j graph and RDF claim-graph projections into the first release, but the design's own evidence (technology-research §1.2/§6: relational + bounded recursive CTE suffices for first release; §18 permits typed REST with no graph engine; T4 C-as-projection is deferred) supports v1 = typed REST query over Postgres + pgvector + tsvector/pg_trgm only. Keep ProjectionBuilder/VectorIndex/query-adapter interfaces as contracts; implement graph/RDF builders only on a measured trigger (unbounded path traversal or RDF interop requirement). Full review: artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-complexity-review.md

title: UMD complexity review: event-sourced ledger is the simplest correct design, keep it
body: Finding (justified complexity, HIGH confidence): the event-sourced semantic ledger + Tier-0/Tier-1 projection split is the simplest correct design for Task.md §2/§7/§15/§21/§29, not the most elaborate. Documented alternatives (mutable Neo4j+changelog, XTDB bitemporal, RDF co-authority) were rejected on evidence (Overeem 8/19 abandonment; Nat Pryce dual-write postmortem). The design draws the right event boundary (semantics in log; deterministic derived evidence in typed tables/OCFL, not events) and the single shared reduce_current_state function correctly collapses Tier-0/Tier-1 divergence risk into one implementation. DDAuthor should resist any 'simplify to direct relational + audit table' argument. Full review: artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-complexity-review.md

title: UMD CI-repair: release E2E surface is vacuous in CI; repair it, don't add surfaces
body: CI-repair complexity review (artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-ci-repair-complexity-review.md). Verified: tests/test_api_boundary_e2e.py contributes ZERO assertions in CI — in-process TestClient over throwaway DB, compose db publishes no port, docker-e2e job never sets UMD_TEST_POSTGRES, and _require_production_path skips on capabilities (which can never be active: app.py:167 wires DurableDAGRunner, capability.py has no connectivity probe). The three live shape tests (test_hatchet_live.py:920-1006) are real bindings (not handoff §6's RecordingClient version) but are executed by NO CI job and use _ok stub work. Highest-leverage simplification: one shared runtime-assembly function used by BOTH app.build_context and cli.worker (cli.py:96 currently builds runtime={"engine": engine} only → worker would run degraded stage work); transport-switch the boundary scenario (TestClient | httpx live) instead of adding a second E2E file.

title: UMD CI-repair: 4 proposed additions are accidental complexity; core is justified
body: Verdict: APPROPRIATE-with-reducible-EXCESS. Core repair (commit 5 mechanical dep/env fixes; fix compose.yaml:104 + hatchet.py:56 image path to sub-path topology; wire existing ProductionDAGRunner seam; pip install .[worker]; real JWT token + server ports; flip UMD_VALIDATE_LIVE_WORKER to mandatory; execute shape tests) is requirement-mandated. Accidental complexity to simplify: (1) Split-Job CI (B) — test-postgres already is the fast loop; path filters drift; not needed. (2) Preflight manifest probes (C) — keep as ~10-line diagnostic step, not a subsystem. (3) T3's submit+poll probe with 30s TTL cache — probe is disclosure, tests are the gate; skip the cache machinery. (4) UMD_EXECUTION_BACKEND env axis — prefer env-derived runner selection. D (Lite) correctly dropped for topology skew (R4 same-stack evidence). Tag uncertainty: T5-T8 of the adversarial log are NOT yet on disk (log ends after T4's persisting risks) — DD must not be finalized from a 4-turn debate.

title: UMD CI-repair post-T8: design APPROPRIATE, five execution gaps block release evidence
body: Verdict: APPROPRIATE-with-residual-EXCESS. The 8-turn adversarial design is minimal and correct (one scheduler, one split topology, one reachability-only probe, one E2E transport, no split-job, Lite dead, fail-on-skip allowlist). Residual excess is implementation-vs-design drift, verified in tree: (1) cli.worker builds runtime={"engine": engine} while app.build_context assembles 16 deps — worker would run degraded stage work; DD's 'one shared runtime assembly' written but not executed. (2) validation.yml:214 still UMD_VALIDATE_LIVE_WORKER:-false opt-in gate. (3) No CapabilityProbe exists → /v1/capabilities can never be active → boundary E2E _require_production_path still skips (vacuous gate risk). (4) No E2E transport switch (UMD_LIVE_API_URL/httpx absent; restart test builds second create_app, contradicting DD live-mode rule). (5) app.py:167 still wires DurableDAGRunner (dual-runner window, bounded only by rewire-with-gate-flip). Plus LOW: stale Plan I QA note calling shape tests RecordingClient-defective when committed file is real client. Full review: artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-ci-repair-complexity-review-t8.md

title: UMD CI-repair: justified-complexity keep-list validated post-T8 (split topology, SDK pre-alignment, single retry authority, allowlist fail-on-skip)
body: Validated keep-list (each traceable to Task.md/CONTRACTS/R4): Hatchet sole scheduler + ProductionDAGRunner (Task.md §23, CONTRACTS:61); compose split topology migrate→admin→engine+dashboard + Postgres msgqueue + per-run token minting (R4 same-stack, Lite correctly dead); SDK v1 surface pre-alignment with mandatory surface-contract tests (F1 — converts first-run discovery into hermetic failure); retry ownership single authority executor-only with Hatchet retries=0 + NonRetryable (F2); CapabilityProbe = one reachability call via injected client, cached+hysteresis, disclosure-not-gate (F4); fail-on-skip allowlist hook + always-run gate job (F6/B-1); manifest-inspect preflight tripwire ~10 lines (C-2); restart segments with named volumes; pin surfaces (4) enforced by pair-agreement test (correct rewrite of unsatisfiable single-string assertion); runner set justified because ProductionDAGRunner+HatchetRunner share submit_workflow_runs (no duplicated submission path). Product-vs-CI split CLEAN at design level; gate closure NOT achieved (correctly, no hosted run); no-skips design sound but mechanism unbuilt; 6 topology proofs are named first-run observations, no machinery. Simplification advice: do NOT further reduce the justified core; close F1-F5 execution gaps instead.

title: UMD CI-repair: reconcile loop conflates netns race (332280) with optional-sandbox/one-shot misclassification (332283)
body: Complexity review of the plan-K netns amendment. Two failure classes must not share one blind retry loop. Class A (run 33228084721): TRUE daemon netns race (bind-mount /proc/PID/ns/net -> /var/run/docker/netns/...: no such file or directory). Current grep gate matches the signature but reconcile's 5 plain re-ups cannot recover a half-created container with a dead netns — retry must remove the victim container (docker compose rm -sf / docker rm -f) before re-up; mechanism MEDIUM confidence (consistent with 5 failed re-ups). Class B (run 33228376245): NO daemon error; sandbox-runner=restarting is DETERMINISTIC (compose sandbox-runner env lacks UMD_HATCHET_SERVER_URL/TOKEN — they exist only on api/worker lines 79-81/120-122; cli.worker fail-closes exit 2; restart: unless-stopped crash-loops, compounded by R17 seccomp EPERM) and hatchet-migrate/admin=absent is a ps-classification artifact (two instantiation modes: up -d tracked vs run --rm oneoff removed). Findings: (1) HIGH sandbox-runner must leave required_running (compose OPTIONAL 223-235; ledger; and giving it a token would register a SECOND umd-worker -> duplicate callbacks/retry multiplication -> violates SOLE-execution-target + C1/C5). (2) HIGH one-shot completion cannot come from ps -a -q/state=exited; require docker inspect ExitCode==0; completion already fail-closed twice via compose service_completed_successfully + fail-closed token mint (298-301). (3) HIGH no retry on restarting/absent (deterministic); retry only on netns signature. (4) HIGH record-release-summary.sh:73 claims sandbox 'Required' — must say OPTIONAL/diagnostic. (5) diagnostics must add per-service ExitCode/RestartCount/ps-json/reconcile observation table. Scope: only validation.yml startup step + capture-diagnostics.sh (+ small reconcile-stack.sh helper) + 1 summary line; product stream unchanged; no gate weakening.

title: One-shot completion is already fail-closed by compose service_completed_successfully + token-mint step; ps-based reconcile re-derivation is redundant complexity
body: In the validation.yml reconcile loop, hatchet-migrate/hatchet-admin completion is re-derived from `docker compose ps -a -q` presence + state=exited. This machinery is redundant: (a) compose itself encodes success via depends_on: service_completed_successfully on hatchet-admin->migrate and engine/dashboard->admin+migrate (compose.yaml 173,195-198,215-218), and (b) the "Start config generation... mint real tenant JWT" step already fail-closes (exit 1) if /hatchet/config or tenant discovery or token minting fails (validation.yml 248-307). The ps-based classification adds a false-failure surface (run 332283 reported hatchet-migrate=absent hatchet-admin=absent) without adding evidence. Simplest correct design: keep the config step as the one-shot gate, record canonical-container ExitCode+logs as diagnostics, and remove ps-presence from the decision path.

title: Plan K netns amendment: APPROPRIATE-with-reducible-EXCESS (4 simplifications)
body: Complexity review of the validated adversarial artifact (F1-F10 + U1-U8) written to artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-plan-k-netns-complexity-review.md. Core amendment is evidence-justified (R15/R16/R17/R18); every mandatory mechanism preserved. Four bounded simplifications proposed that keep L1-L9 intact: F-A drop B' single-owner wrapper (single serial job makes it a new failure surface; JWT mint stays a workflow step, killing F6 own-process export + U5 verdict-on-death-path); F-B drop docker wait + timeout 300 (inspect polling in bounded reconcile already sufficient); F-C cut preflight Class A daemon-reachability wait (runner images always have daemon up; zero hosted evidence of cold daemon); F-D reduce per-batch reconcile to batch wait, full-set reconcile stays the gate. F-E merge Batch 1 (db) into config-phase Batch 1 (3 invocations total). Prior L9 finding superseded: R15/R18 prove ps-based reconcile-as-gate IS justified; what was redundant was its blind re-up implementation (validation.yml:375-377 || true), which F7's classified re-up fixes.

title: B' wrapper is the root cause of two other complexity items
body: The single-owner compose wrapper (B') in the Plan K netns amendment is the root cause of F6's own-process JWT export and U5's verdict-on-death-path: both exist only because the JWT mint and Batch 4 share one step. Keeping the mint as a separate workflow step (it already is today, validation.yml:248-307, GITHUB_ENV already reaches subsequent steps) eliminates both requirements. Serial steps already make concurrent compose invocations structurally impossible, so the wrapper's only structural justification (prevent concurrency) is theoretical in a single-job workflow. Simplest shape: compose ownership stays in workflow steps with the U1 shielding idiom; classification helper is a small grep function, not a state machine.

title: Plan K netns amendment: core justified, ~1/3 reducible, U1 pattern-text defect BLOCKING
body: Durable review at artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-plan-k-netns-complexity-review.md. Verdict: ELEVATED complexity, justified=true. Workflow-only amendment (F1-F10 + F-R18) is the correct decision; core (exact-marker anchored retry, fail-closed reconcile 2d84d07, status-capture correctness, first-exit one-shot classifier, EPERM sandbox classification, umd-evidence schema + escalation verdict, R18 caveat) is evidence-backed and must ship. Reducible excess (S2-S9): four batches -> two-phase with --no-deps + COMPOSE_PARALLEL_LIMIT=1 + tripwire; per-batch 3x4 budget -> one shared 3-attempt budget; drop F2 Class A daemon-wait 120s/5s (class unobserved in R10-R18; preflight-hatchet-images.sh covers Class B image half); drop docker wait + timeout 300 (duplicates existing config-poll/tenant-poll/JWT-mint fail-closed signals); scope bash contract to compose-owning scripts (kills U3 AT-11 audit); keep JWT mint step boundary (own-process export only needed due to F3 consolidation); Q1-gate sandbox-runner env parity (option-a registers a second umd-worker with different isolation -> product decision). All U1-U8/Q1-Q8 preserved; L1-L9 intact; forbidden set untouched. Verify-before-build gap: R16 5-failed-re-ups may need docker compose rm of marker victim before re-up — observe first green run, don't add rm speculatively.

title: Plan K live Hatchet blocker: APPROPRIATE with 6 rejections + 6 simplifications; fix surface = diagnosed defects only
body: Complexity review at artifacts/designs/process/universal-media-decomposer-plan-k-hatchet-live-blocker-complexity-review.md. Verdict: APPROPRIATE, justified=true. The live-blocker repair (AT-16 handler contract, AT-17 tenant eligibility, AT-18 durable_task, readiness truthfulness, hermetic alignment, honest local-test re-scope, hosted rerun) is evidence-justified and must ship as scoped. REJECT as unnecessary abstraction: R1 v0->v1 payload adapter (no v0 producer exists — runner.py:232-239 emits top-level dict only), R2 fake Context class hierarchy in hermetic tests (handler ignores ctx — placeholder suffices), R3 engine-query machinery in the local cluster test (test_hatchet_live.py:1035-1080 overclaims 'engine-visible'; hosted AT-18 v1_task.is_durable=true owns that proof — re-scope honestly instead), R4 registration retry loop (decoration-time registration is deterministic; fail fast), R5 task<->durable_task dual-path switch (AT-18 fixes the surface), R6 readiness abstraction (only two consumers; tighten the boolean). APPLY simplifications: S1 delete contextlib.suppress at hatchet.py:426 (its 'deferred registration' premise is wrong — decorator inner() executes registration immediately), S2 delete cli.py:123 len(work_registry) fallback (always masks failure), S3 _ready = callbacks_bound and bool(registered_workflows), S4 _invoke_callback -> cb(manifest.to_dict(), ctx), S5 handler -> def handler(payload, ctx) reading payload['manifest'], S6 re-scope local registration test. Residual risks flagged, not built around: N1 durable_task is requirement-interpretation not proven dispatch blocker (L10 was tenant partitions) — keep, don't expand; N2 sync durable handler deprecation warning — keep sync; N3 SDK output serialization of StageRunRecord — verify, no serializer layer. Preserve AT-16-19 verbatim via netns DD reconciliation (do not duplicate); preserve AT-17 tenant-partition + assignment/runtime state (prior defect). Acceptance = AC1-AC9 in the artifact; hosted rerun successor to 33229130339/99038602321 is the release-gate evidence before docs/DoD closure.

title: SDK py/1.38.1 verified first-hand: fn(input, ctx) two-arg arity, direct input, durable_task facade, is_durable flag
body: Fetched pinned hatchet_sdk==1.38.1 source from github.com/hatchet-dev/hatchet tag py/1.38.1 (checked 2026-08-29). Confirmed: (1) Task.call()/aio_call() invoke self._fn(workflow_input, cast(Context, ctx)) — TWO positional args; the run input dict is passed directly, no {"input": ...} wrapper. (2) Task.to_proto() emits is_durable=self._is_durable — client.task registers non-durable tasks; Hatchet.durable_task(*, name=...) exists (hatchet.py), wraps in Workflow.durable_task, hands DurableContext to the handler, and emits a deprecation warning for non-async durable handlers. (3) Hatchet.worker() raises TypeError for non-Workflow/Standalone items. (4) Task has built-in mock_run()/aio_mock_run() unit-test surfaces calling the real two-arg path. Grounds AT-16 (handler(input, ctx) direct shape) and AT-18 (durable_task + is_durable=true) in the actual pinned SDK source, elevating them from debugger/researcher citations to first-hand verification. Also confirms the wrong-arity TypeError would fire at decoration time inside HatchetWorkerFactory.start — where contextlib.suppress at hatchet.py:426 hides it.

title: Plan K live-Hatchet dependency-barrier: Option 1 (single-workflow DAG) recommended; Options 2/3/4 rejected; two human decisions open
body: Complexity review COMPLEXITY-universal-media-decomposer-plan-k-live-hatchet-lineage-barrier.md written (read-only). Verdict ELEVATED. Option 1 (Workflow.durable_task(name, parents=[...])) is the only machinery-minimal architecture: expresses all STAGE_DEPENDENCIES edges, no polling/retry/snapshot, sync handler preserved (R22 stands). Its costs are two bounded reconciliations: (a) AT-18 literal 'client.durable_task per umd-<stage>' vs single-workflow topology (R19) — resolved by contract-text clarification adopting the property reading; (b) readiness count must count tasks (9) not workflow objects (1). Option 2 (parent_step_run_id/pair upgrade) rejected: singular+unproven, cannot express multi-parent, upgrade leg is a coordinated SDK/server migration. Option 3 (snapshot reversal) rejected: reverses P2-S14:105 rejection and snapshot is the proven source of the live-dup 10-vs-9 key defect; stale after rekey. Option 4 (pre-claim retry) rejected as primary: largest new machinery, conflicts with no-polling/no-retry-loop rejections, needs substantial new DD. Shared: assignment proof must use v1_task_events_olap transitions + v1_tasks_olap latest_worker_id (ASSIGNED is NOT a v1 readable status per researcher), one shared proof contract; runner.py:255-258 multi-parent truncation must be repaired regardless. Coverage gap: named eight-turn adversarial artifact ADVERSARIAL-...-lineage-barrier.md does not exist on disk; refiner round in flight. Human decisions H1 (AT-18 reading) and H2 (readiness count semantics) gate selection.

title: Hatchet stack quantified: 4/7 compose services, 7 env vars, 949 CI script lines, ~4.2K test lines — marginal value over existing Postgres job state
body: Independent complexity review of Universeity vs Task.md + pending DDs. Hatchet is the largest non-product block: 4 of 7 default compose services (migrate/admin/engine/dashboard), 7 of 39 env vars, .github/scripts 949 lines, validation.yml 559 lines, test_hatchet_live.py 2112 lines (largest test), hatchet.py 25.4KB + tenant probe discover_runnable_tenant (hatchet.py:100-156) reading third-party Tenant table schema. Meanwhile Task.md §23 durable-job requirements (submit/poll/cancel/retry/rerun/restart/no-repeat) are ALREADY implemented in Postgres: stage_run UNIQUE idempotency claim + job.cancelled_stages + job_run_audit + DurableStageExecutor (stage_execution.py:168-519) + DurableDAGRunner (runner.py:66-150). Hatchet itself is Postgres-queued (SERVER_MSGQUEUE_KIND=postgres). Mandate-bound: DD CI-repair C1, netns L9, live-blocker L10 all require Hatchet as sole v1 scheduler — a Postgres-queue swap needs DD supersession, not implementation. Disposition: KEEP under constraints; document Postgres-queue fallback as minimal architecture.

title: PhaseE test-coupled block: 1965 src lines with zero production callers
body: umd/recovery/ocfl_backup.py (150), recovery/postgres_backup.py (402), operations/controller.py (307), operations/vector_ops.py (92), operations/runbooks.py (159), projections/publish.py ProjectionPublishManager (281), jobs/drain.py (107) are imported ONLY by tests (test_recovery_phaseE, test_operational_phaseE, test_vector_ops_phaseE, test_observability_phaseE, test_drain, test_deployment_phaseE — 1058 test lines). SimpleUniverseGate (drain.py) is a test double for a DAG-universe gate production never instantiates (no API endpoint, no startup hook). Violates the DD's own "projection builders implement only on measured trigger" doctrine. Disposition: defer/delete until a consumer exists. Confidence: HIGH unwired, MEDIUM deletion (backup/restore may be deliberately staged ops).

title: The Postgres queue already exists in-repo: DurableDAGRunner + DurableStageExecutor are a complete durable executor without Hatchet
body: The candidate "Postgres queue" simplification is not hypothetical — the codebase already contains a working Postgres-backed durable DAG runner (runner.py:66-150 DurableDAGRunner over DurableStageExecutor + PostgresJobRepository, wired via app.py runner="hermetic"). Every Task.md §23 behavior (idempotent claim via UNIQUE(idempotency_key), retry/quarantine, restart-resume via _replayed_complete, cancel via job.cancelled_stages, rerun via invalidation planner, no-repeat-after-failure via committed_prior_refs) is tested hermetically through Postgres in test_hatchet_live.py's postgres-marked tests. A production Postgres-queue worker = a lease loop (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED over stage_run pending rows, ~200-300 new lines) + re-claim-on-start. That replaces 4 compose services, hatchet.py adapter, capability probe, tenant discovery, JWT minting, engine-visible-proof script, AT-16/17/18 apparatus. Blocked only by approved-DD mandates (C1/L9/L10), not by engineering feasibility.
